## TL;DR

Fixed the release email summary bug identified in review: bullet highlights now use the opening sentence as their detail, so text after the first sentence cannot replace or misstate the change. Added table-driven regression cases for multi-sentence and single-sentence bullets. The required scoped RepoOS check passed after correcting one test expectation about preserved punctuation.

## Work and rationale

The release email summary is derived by `noteItems` in `src/server/release-email.ts`. The parser extracts concise names and details from both heading-led paragraphs and Markdown bullets. Review identified that the bullet path set `detail` from the text after the first sentence. For notes such as `- Fix boot. Also improves recovery.`, the name came from “Fix boot” while the detail became “Also improves recovery.” The highlight and TL;DR could therefore emphasize a secondary statement instead of describing the change named by the bullet.

I changed the detail selection so a bullet uses its opening sentence. The rest of the extraction logic stays intact: section paragraphs continue to use the first sentence when a meaningful heading supplies the feature name, and generic prose keeps its existing fallback behavior. This keeps the repair local to the faulty source shape without changing the full release notes or other summary formatting.

In `src/ui-app/tests/release-email.test.ts`, I replaced the regression expectation that locked in the incorrect remainder sentence with table-driven examples. The cases cover a bullet with two sentences, a bullet with three sentences, and a one-sentence bullet without terminal punctuation. They assert the name and detail returned by `summarizeReleaseNotes`, the output consumed by the email highlights and TL;DR. Existing paragraph-based summary assertions remain in place.

## Approaches tried

I traced the review finding through all uses of `noteItems`, `splitSentence`, and summary details. There was one bullet-specific instance of the faulty selection in this helper; other matches for `detail` in the server tree were unrelated parsing or delivery code. I kept the same `splitSentence` extraction and selected its `first` value for bullets, rather than changing the splitter or reducing all note forms to one generic rule. That preserves the heading-sensitive behavior of paragraph notes.

I first ran the required `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check`. Its remote run isolated a failure in the new test: the single-sentence case expected a trailing period even though the existing helper preserves the punctuation supplied by the notes. I reproduced the named test locally, confirmed the actual output, and corrected only that expected string. The next scoped check completed successfully. The remote runner reported all changed-path tests passing, and the local check plan reported build, formatting, lint, rendered contrast audit, UI smoke, and other applicable checks passed.

## Challenges and blockers

The first required check failed because of the test expectation, not the code behavior under review. The output clarified that one-sentence bullet details are not automatically punctuated; retaining authored punctuation is consistent with the existing summary implementation, so the test now expects the unpunctuated source text. The repository check also retried remote validation after two hosts failed their network throughput probes. A third host completed the run, so there was no remaining infrastructure blocker.

RepoOS creates a WIP checkpoint during scoped checks. After the first run, the tracked source files were read-only in the worktree; I restored owner write permission before correcting the test and rerunning the gate. No manual commit or main-checkout edit was made.

## Key learnings

Each Markdown shape that feeds summary copy needs direct coverage. A shared sentence splitter does not ensure equivalent details when callers select different parts of its result. A regression test should verify the final item returned by the summary helper, because that is the value shown in both the highlights and TL;DR.

Summary extraction should remain separate from the complete changelog rendering. The summary needs a concise, faithful excerpt, while the complete notes preserve all technical context. Fixing a summary selector should not rewrite or truncate the release notes below it.
